title: The Son of God, the ever-living fountain of light

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 11, col. D, to p. 12, col. A (PDF pp. 35-36)

source_text: Spiritus Sanctus superveniet in te, et virtus Altissimi obumbrabit tibi: ideo et quod nascetur ex te sanctum, vocabitur Filius Dei. Si autem Filius Dei, etiam Deus, eiusdem formae cum Patre, et coaeternus: in quo omnem Pater possidet clarificationem: character atque imago in persona; et per splendorem gloria refulget. Et quemadmodum ex perenni fonte procedunt flumina: sic et ex hoc perenni ac semper vivo fonte, progreditur perennis et vera lux mundi, Christus Deus noster. De eo namque Prophetae clamarunt: Fluminis impetus laetificat civitatem Dei: neque unam duntaxat civitatem, sed omnes; nam sicut unam civitatem, universum terrarum laetificat orbem.
pass_a_gloss: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you: therefore also what will be born of you holy, will be called Son of God. But if Son of God, also God (Deus), of the same form (eiusdem formae) with the Father, and coeternal (coaeternus): in whom the Father possesses (possidet) all glorification (clarificatio): impress/stamp (character) and image (imago) in person (in persona); and through radiance (per splendorem) glory (gloria) shines back/out (refulget). And just as from an everlasting spring (perennis fons) rivers (flumina) proceed (procedunt): so also from this everlasting and ever-living (semper vivus) spring proceeds (progreditur) the everlasting and true light of the world (vera lux mundi), Christ our God. For about Him the Prophets cried out (clamarunt): The rush of the river (fluminis impetus) gladdens (laetificat) the city of God (civitas Dei): and not one city only (duntaxat), but all; for as one city, the whole circle of lands it gladdens.

choices.issue: character atque imago in persona ... per splendorem gloria
choices.choice: 'character atque imago in persona ... per splendorem gloria' reflects Hebrews 1:3 (Greek charakter tes hypostaseos, apaugasma tes doxes); cited.
'imago' may also recall Colossians 1:15 and 'eiusdem formae' Philippians 2:6; not cited separately.
'in persona' rendered 'in His own person' rather than 'of His person', which would import Hebrews 1:3 wording the Latin does not have;
'per splendorem gloria refulget' kept as 'through the radiance the glory shines out' (no added 'through Him, as').
'vera lux mundi' joins John 1:9 (true light) and John 8:12 (light of the world); both cited.
The ascription 'De eo namque Prophetae clamarunt' is plural in the print and kept as 'the prophets'.

pass_b_english: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the holy one who will be born of you will also be called the Son of God (Luke 1:35). But if He is the Son of God, He is also God, of the same form as the Father and coeternal with Him. In Him the Father possesses all glory; He is, in His own person, the imprint and the image, and through the radiance the glory shines out (Hebrews 1:3).

And as rivers flow from an ever-flowing spring, so from this ever-flowing and ever-living spring comes forth the everlasting and true Light of the world, Christ our God (John 1:9; John 8:12). For of Him the prophets cried out: The rush of the river makes glad the city of God (Psalm 46:4). And not one city only, but all; for it gladdens the whole world as though it were one city.
notes: Margin 'Psal. 45' is Vulgate numbering: Vulgate Psalm 45:5 = Psalm 46:4 in English Bibles; English numbering used in the citation. 'character atque imago in persona ... per splendorem gloria' reflects Hebrews 1:3 (Greek charakter tes hypostaseos, apaugasma tes doxes); cited. 'imago' may also recall Colossians 1:15 and 'eiusdem formae' Philippians 2:6; not cited separately. 'clarificatio' rendered 'glory'. 'in persona' rendered 'in His own person' rather than 'of His person', which would import Hebrews 1:3 wording the Latin does not have; 'per splendorem gloria refulget' kept as 'through the radiance the glory shines out' (no added 'through Him, as'). 'vera lux mundi' joins John 1:9 (true light) and John 8:12 (light of the world); both cited. The ascription 'De eo namque Prophetae clamarunt' is plural in the print and kept as 'the prophets'.
